title: Abuse protection and privacy-preserving analytics
summary: Harden the existing service in three confirmed ways: throttle each client (strictly for link creation, loosely for redirects), refuse destinations that are internal, disguised, self-referencing or blocklisted, and extend statistics with unique-visitor and top-referrer aggregates while storing nothing that identifies a visitor.

functional.statement: Link creation is rate limited per client.
acceptance_criteria: More than the configured number of creations per minute from one client returns 429 with a Retry-After header and a problem document
The limit is configurable and can be disabled; clients have independent budgets
X-Forwarded-For identifies the client only when the deployment declares a trusted proxy

functional.statement: Redirects are rate limited per client with a separate, looser budget.
acceptance_criteria: Exceeding the redirect budget returns 429 and the refused visit is not counted as a click
Health probes and read-only API calls are never limited

functional.statement: Unsafe destinations are refused when a link is created.
acceptance_criteria: Loopback, private, link-local and otherwise non-public addresses are refused in every spelling browsers accept
Internal host names, URLs with embedded credentials and URLs pointing back at the service are refused
Domains on a configurable blocklist, and their subdomains, are refused
Refusals return 422 with a reason; ordinary public URLs are unaffected

functional.statement: Statistics report unique visitors and top referrers.
acceptance_criteria: The per-day breakdown includes the number of distinct visitors that day
Statistics list the most frequent referring hosts

non_functional.statement: Privacy: no personal data about visitors is persisted or logged.
acceptance_criteria: No IP address or user agent is stored or written to logs
Visitor identifiers cannot be reversed to an address and cannot be linked across days
Only the host of a referrer is stored, never its path or query string

non_functional.statement: Bounded resources: protections use constant time and bounded memory.
acceptance_criteria: Rate-limit state never exceeds a fixed number of tracked clients
Per-request overhead does not grow with the number of clients or clicks

non_functional.statement: Backward compatibility with existing links, clients and data.
acceptance_criteria: Existing response fields are unchanged; new fields are additive
Existing links and previously recorded clicks keep working and still aggregate
Safe defaults: limits on, forwarded headers untrusted, empty blocklist

assumptions.statement: The three concerns are independent and ship together as one hardening release.
Q1 answered: 'hammered' means abusive clients, not organic growth. Rate-limit per client; creation is the abuse vector, redirects get a much looser limit. No caching or scale-out in this change.
Q2 answered: rule-based blocking only. No external reputation service this quarter; a configurable blocklist covers known bad domains.
Q3 answered: aggregates only. Product needs unique visitors and top referrers; storing IP addresses, user agents or location is explicitly rejected.
Rate limits are enforced per instance; the service currently runs as a single instance.

out_of_scope: Retroactive vetting of links that already exist
